_meta.what: Row-by-row review of the 128 n8n daily-signal rows (May–Sep 2026) and the repo's own briefs, done 5 Sep 2026 after the MD saw the first app export and said several entries 'look irrelevant and bad' (TDK, Disney+, Nissan …). Applied at export time (intel/site_export.py) — the database keeps every row; the app shows screened rows under 'Screened out' with the reason, collapses duplicates into the kept row, and tags rows that still need a human check.
_meta.how: Each row was checked against: the live sponsor table (existing F1/FE partner → screened), the blocklist and the approached list, the ICP (B2B, deal-capable, capacity ≥ $1B valuation or $100M ARR or public), whether the row is a rights-holder/team/broadcaster rather than a prospect, duplicate entries of the same trigger, and obvious data faults (undisclosed decision-maker, wrong source, inconsistent facts).
_meta.statuses: screened_out (with reason code) · duplicate_of (kept key) · keep_flagged (needs a human check before it is shown as a clean signal) · keep (default for anything not listed)

reason_codes.existing_partner: already an F1 / FE / team partner (sponsor table or the row itself says so)
reason_codes.rights_holder: a team, the championship, a broadcaster or a supplier — not a prospect
reason_codes.approached: already approached by the 1440 team — never re-pitch cold
reason_codes.off_profile: consumer / B2C, or a category with no B2B sponsorship logic
reason_codes.no_trigger: no capital or leadership event — an association, not a signal
reason_codes.below_capacity: fails the capacity gate (valuation < $1B and no $100M ARR / listing)
reason_codes.too_early: seed / first institutional money; brand budget not there yet
reason_codes.category_conflict: conflicts with a supplier category the series already locks (tyres, fuel)

_meta.key: date|company (company as recorded); matched case-insensitively on the normalised company name

2026-07-01|Joulent.reason: contradicted: The event is real and inside the window, but the signal as recorded does not survive the primary source. The thin row read it as a $1.75B venture-style 'strategic financing' of an 'AI-compute energy infrastructure' company suited to Formula E. The company release (Business Wire, 1 Jul 2026) and National Grid's own release (PR Newswire, 1 Jul 2026) say National Grid Ventures agreed to invest $1.75B for a 35% equity stake in Joulent LLC, a Houston developer of natural-gas power plants that launched from stealth on 22 Jun 2026 after three years of incubation inside Engine No. 1. Its flagship, Project Kilby, is a ~2.67 GW gas-fired facility in West Texas, a 50/50 venture with Chevron, supplying a Microsoft-operated data-centre campus under a 20-year PPA with GE Vernova turbines and first power targeted for 2028. So: (1) the capital is a utility buying into project equity, not a growth round that funds brand-building; (2) the business is gas-fired baseload generation for one hyperscaler customer, which contradicts the Formula E sustainability positioning the row assumed and leaves no consumer or broad-B2B audience a sponsorship would reach; (3) the leadership found (Chris James, Founder & CEO, also founder of Engine No. 1; Brian Boland, EVP, CFO & Head of Strategy; Chris Wissel-Tyson, SVP Growth & Strategy; Noah Tulsky, VP Corporate Development) shows no marketing or brand function, and no motorsport tie was found for any of them. Scored honestly on the five pillars (capacity from project finance, weak brand fit, no urgency beyond the 2026 Chevron FID, no on-car or operational workstream) the company sits well below the 70 threshold, so a built case would be a plausible-sounding company with a logo. Re-open only if Joulent itself announces a corporate brand programme or an F1-relevant energy technology (e.g. trackside power) rather than plant development.
